description: Phase-WIKI-FIX — substrate bug sweep surfaced by 2026-05-22 direct /api/wiki/search bench. Ten distinct bugs identified, consolidated into 8 atomic stories. Bench numbers (from inside docker network): p50=17ms, p95=55ms — latency fine. Recall@5 ~90-100% — substrate finds. BUT score 0.013 uniform across 20 queries → fusion gira ma con 1/3 canali perché `SELECT count(*) FROM wiki_documents` = 17 vs 150+ pages on disk. FTS5 mirror stale. Plus 8 step manuali per bumpare EMBEDDING_OUTPUT_DIM 256→768 (settings updated_at constraint, no auto-detect dim mismatch, embed n_ctx hard-cap 1024, rebuild bails on first error, cache key non include dim, no admin reindex endpoint, system page leak, davide ×2). Tutti substrate bugs, NESSUNO è agent loop. Phase-WIKI-FIX è priority-0 blocker per Phase-WIKI-B Wave A — RRF su FTS vuota = RRF su 1 canale = misurazione inutile della fusion. Plan + acceptance + verification probes per story: .planning/post-drift-2026-05-21/Phase-WIKI-FIX/plan.md. STRICT one-story-exit per scripts/ralph/CLAUDE.md.

userStories.title: FTS5 mirror auto-sync on wiki write/delete
userStories.description: Today SELECT count(*) FROM wiki_documents = 17 (mostly legacy graph:node:* entries) while wiki disk has 150+ pages and Qdrant has 290 points. The hybrid fusion mergeHybridResults already wires 3 channels (exact, FTS, vector) into /api/wiki/search via SearchHybrid, but the FTS channel returns zero because the SQLite FTS5 mirror is empty/stale. This story makes the FTS5 mirror update SYNCHRONOUSLY in the same write transaction as WritePage/DeletePage. (a) AUDIT: grep `wiki_documents` writes — there's likely a writer in internal/storage/search/sqlite.go and possibly stale paths in internal/reindex/. Centralize into a single helper if currently scattered. (b) HOOK: internal/wiki/store_writes.go atomic write path must call FTS5 upsert. Existing Qdrant submitter is already wired (`s.SetReindexSubmitter(rw)`); the FTS5 sync should be IN-PROCESS sibling, not via the reindex worker (Qdrant is rebuildable; FTS5 mirror is authoritative for the FTS channel and must not lag). (c) DELETE PATH: same hook for DeletePage — remove the row immediately. (d) BOOT RECONCILER: on `wiki.NewStore` boot, count `wiki_documents` rows vs on-disk pages — if drift > 5%, log warning and trigger full rebuild from disk. (e) REGRESSION TEST: integration test in internal/wiki/store_writes_test.go that writes a page, calls `wiki_documents MATCH '<title token>'`, asserts hit. Delete the page, assert MATCH returns 0 rows.
acceptanceCriteria: internal/wiki/store_writes.go WritePage triggers FTS5 upsert in the SAME function call (not via a goroutine), before returning
internal/wiki/store_writes.go DeletePage triggers FTS5 row removal
Boot reconciler in wiki.NewStore (or a small helper called from there) detects mirror drift and rebuilds from disk; logged with `wiki: FTS5 mirror rebuilt`
After running aura with all 150+ wiki pages on disk: docker exec aura-aura-1 sqlite3 /data/aura.db 'SELECT count(*) FROM wiki_documents' returns ≥ on-disk page count minus system pages
MATCH probe: docker exec aura-aura-1 sqlite3 /data/aura.db "SELECT id FROM wiki_documents WHERE wiki_documents MATCH 'galileo' LIMIT 3" returns galileo-galilei AND related pages
Bench rerun (per memory project_2026-05-22_substrate_bench_diagnosis) shows score_fts > 0 on ≥15/20 queries (today: 0/20)
go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./internal/wiki/... ./internal/storage/search/... -count=1 green
Single atomic commit prefix: fix(wiki): auto-sync FTS5 mirror on page write/delete (US-WIKI-FIX-01)
userStories.notes: HIGHEST IMPACT STORY in the phase. Without this, every other fix (dedup, system filter, reindex endpoint) measures against a degenerate fusion (vector-only). GROUND-TRUTH BEFORE EDIT: (1) grep -rn 'wiki_documents' internal/storage/search/ internal/wiki/ to find all write paths. (2) Read internal/storage/search/sqlite.go in full — the FTS5 schema + existing writers live there. (3) Read internal/wiki/store_writes.go WritePage + DeletePage paths. (4) Check internal/reindex/ — is there a worker that's SUPPOSED to keep wiki_documents fresh? Maybe the worker exists but only listens on graph rebuild events, not page writes. (5) Audit: is the 17-entry stale state because the OLD schema was `graph:node:<slug>` prefixed and the migration to new schema never repopulated? If yes, this story includes the migration. SCOPE DISCIPLINE: NO changes to the hybrid fusion code (mergeHybridResults stays as-is). NO changes to Qdrant. NO new tools. Only the FTS5 mirror sync.

userStories.title: settings.updated_at default to CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
userStories.description: Today INSERT INTO settings(key, value) VALUES(...) fails with 'NOT NULL constraint failed: settings.updated_at'. Witnessed during 2026-05-22 dim bump — operator forced to write `INSERT ... VALUES('K','V', datetime('now'))` instead of the natural form. Trivial fix: ALTER COLUMN settings.updated_at DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP via new migration. Sqlite ALTER COLUMN is limited; the migration may need to recreate the table (rename old, create new with default, INSERT SELECT, drop old, rename new). Standard sqlite migration pattern. Also applies to other timestamp columns with NOT NULL without default — audit and fix in same migration.
acceptanceCriteria: New migration file in internal/db/migrations/ with predictable ID prefix
After migration: sqlite3 ... "INSERT INTO settings(key, value) VALUES('TEST_KEY','TEST_VALUE')" succeeds without specifying updated_at
Existing settings rows preserved with their original updated_at values
Migration test in internal/db/migrations/migrations_test.go covers the new defaults
go test ./internal/db/... -count=1 green
Audit comment in migration body lists which other tables/columns had NOT NULL-no-default — fix them in the same migration or scope-defer with explicit list
Single atomic commit prefix: fix(db): settings.updated_at default to CURRENT_TIMESTAMP (US-WIKI-FIX-07)
userStories.notes: GROUND-TRUTH BEFORE EDIT: (1) Read internal/db/migrations/migrations.go to see the migration registry pattern + numbering scheme. (2) `sqlite3 /data/aura.db '.schema settings'` already done — confirmed updated_at NOT NULL no default. (3) Sqlite ALTER COLUMN limitation: must use rename+recreate trick. (4) Check if any code explicitly relies on updated_at being NOT NULL — likely yes (read-side parses it as time.Time). Default = NULL would break that; CURRENT_TIMESTAMP is safe.

userStories.title: Wiki rebuild skip-and-continue on per-page embed error
userStories.description: internal/storage/search/qdrant.go rebuildQdrantWikiDocumentsWithClient (around line 414) bails on the FIRST embed error: `return QdrantRebuildReport{}, fmt.Errorf('embedding %s: %w', doc.ID, err)`. Witnessed live 2026-05-22: one wiki page exceeds embed sidecar context size (1247 tokens vs 1024 limit) → entire wiki collection left empty. Fix: log + skip + continue, accumulate skipped docs in the report. Result: index has best-effort coverage, operator sees what was skipped, can drill in.
acceptanceCriteria: QdrantRebuildReport grows a SkippedDocs []SkippedDoc{DocID string, Reason string} field
rebuild loop catches per-doc embed error, logs `logger.Warn('rebuild: skipping doc', 'id', doc.ID, 'error', err)`, appends to SkippedDocs, continues
Final error is returned ONLY if zero docs were indexed (all skipped); otherwise nil error + report contains skipped list
Vector size consistency check still applies — first SUCCESSFULLY embedded doc sets vectorSize; subsequent mismatches are still hard errors (different from embed-failed)
Test in internal/storage/search/qdrant_test.go (or wherever rebuild tests live) with mock embedFn that fails for one specific doc — assert other docs indexed + skipped doc in report
go test ./internal/storage/search/... -count=1 green
Single atomic commit prefix: fix(qdrant): skip-and-continue on per-page embed error during rebuild (US-WIKI-FIX-03)
userStories.notes: GROUND-TRUTH BEFORE EDIT: Read internal/storage/search/qdrant.go lines 470-525. The current return-on-error pattern is at line ~484. The vector-size mismatch check at line ~491 is DIFFERENT — that one should stay a hard error (it indicates a config drift, not a content-length problem). SCOPE: only the per-doc embed failure path. Do not refactor the dim-mismatch path; that's FIX-04.

userStories.title: Embed sidecar n_ctx default sane + boot smoke
userStories.description: Embed sidecar llama-server declares `--ctx-size 2048` in compose.yaml but the EFFECTIVE per-slot n_ctx is 1024 because `--parallel 2` divides the budget. Witnessed live 2026-05-22 when a 1247-token wiki page hit `embeddings returned 400 Bad Request: input is larger than max context size (1024)`. Fix: (a) bump compose.yaml to `--ctx-size 4096 --batch-size 4096 --ubatch-size 4096` so per-slot is 2048 (matches the model's native n_ctx); (b) document the per-slot math in a comment next to the command; (c) add a boot smoke probe in aura-init-models (or aura itself at startup) that hits `http://aura-llama-embed:8080/props`, asserts default_generation_settings.n_ctx ≥ 2048, refuses to start if not. The compose.yaml bump is already on disk from the 2026-05-22 manual session — confirm + add the probe + add the comment.
acceptanceCriteria: compose.yaml `--ctx-size`, `--batch-size`, `--ubatch-size` all set to 4096 (or higher); comment above the command explains: per-slot n_ctx = ctx-size / parallel
Boot smoke probe (aura-init-models OR a new dedicated check) hits /props on llama-embed, asserts effective n_ctx ≥ 2048, fails fast if not
Smoke probe documented in INSTALL.md or compose.yaml comment
Live: docker compose up -d aura-llama-embed; curl http://localhost:8081/props returns default_generation_settings.n_ctx >= 2048
Embed of a 1500-token wiki page succeeds (was 400 before)
Single atomic commit prefix: chore(embed): n_ctx per-slot math + boot smoke (US-WIKI-FIX-08)
userStories.notes: Lightest story; mostly comments + one probe. The actual ctx-size bump may already be on disk — verify via `grep ctx-size compose.yaml`. If yes, the story collapses to: probe + comment + verify.

userStories.title: Embed cache key includes output_dim
userStories.description: embedding_cache PK today = (content_sha, model). When EMBEDDING_OUTPUT_DIM changes (256 → 768 or vice-versa) the cache returns OLD vectors at OLD dim, failing the rebuild consistency check (`returned vector size 768, want 256`) or worse poisoning Qdrant with mixed-dim points. Witnessed live 2026-05-22 — operator had to DELETE FROM embedding_cache manually after dim swap. Fix: extend cache key to (content_sha, model, output_dim) via SQLite migration. Legacy rows tagged with output_dim=0 OR with current cfg dim on best-effort basis (migration logs the choice).
acceptanceCriteria: New migration adds `output_dim INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` column to embedding_cache
Migration recreates the table (sqlite limit on ALTER PK): old PK (content_sha, model) → new PK (content_sha, model, output_dim)
Legacy rows preserved with output_dim=0 (sentinel for unknown); subsequent reads treat output_dim=0 as cache-miss (force re-embed) so we don't accidentally serve wrong-dim vectors
internal/storage/search/embed_cache.go lookup path takes output_dim parameter; writer path stores it
Migration test green
Test: insert two vectors at sha='X' model='Y' dim=256 then dim=768 → 2 rows; lookup at dim=256 returns 256d; lookup at dim=768 returns 768d
Live: bump EMBEDDING_OUTPUT_DIM via DB UPDATE, restart aura, observe re-embed happens (cache miss because legacy dim=0) NOT crash on dim mismatch
go test ./internal/storage/search/... ./internal/db/... -count=1 green
Single atomic commit prefix: fix(embed): include output_dim in cache key (US-WIKI-FIX-02)
userStories.notes: GROUND-TRUTH BEFORE EDIT: (1) Read internal/storage/search/embed_cache.go fully — it's only ~300 LOC. (2) `.schema embedding_cache` already known: (content_sha, model, embedding BLOB, created_at, PK (content_sha, model)). (3) Migration recipe: ATTACH new schema, INSERT SELECT, DROP old, RENAME — standard pattern visible in existing migrations. (4) The lookup function probably has signature Embed(content) — needs to grow Embed(content, outputDim) OR read outputDim from cfg via the cache constructor. Pick the cleaner one.

userStories.title: Filter system/internal pages out of default /api/wiki/search
userStories.description: Pages tagged with frontmatter category=system (aura-operating-memory, aura-quality-bench, future wiki-index, etc.) leak into normal user search results. Witnessed: `wiki-dante q2` top-1 is `aura-operating-memory` (a system page about Aura's own memory architecture, irrelevant to a Dante question). Fix: (a) at the /api/wiki/search handler, filter results where frontmatter.category == 'system' OR tags contains 'system'; (b) expose ?include_system=1 query param for dashboard/debug use; (c) audit currently-known system pages and add the category if missing.
acceptanceCriteria: Default GET /api/wiki/search?q=dante does NOT return any result with frontmatter.category == 'system'
GET /api/wiki/search?q=dante&include_system=1 includes them (verifies the filter is wired, not hardcoded)
internal/api/wiki.go handleWikiSearch reads ?include_system query param, defaults false, passes to search backend
Search backends (internal/storage/search/) accept the option and filter at result time (or earlier if cheap)

Audit list documented in commit body: which pages had no category and got tagged system? At minimum aura-operating-memory, aura-quality-bench, aura-source-extraction. Apply the frontmatter change atomically with the code change
Bench re-run: no system-tagged page appears in any default top-5 result
go test ./internal/api/... ./internal/storage/search/... -count=1 green
Single atomic commit prefix: feat(wiki): filter system-category pages from default search (US-WIKI-FIX-05)
userStories.notes: DEPENDS ON FIX-01: this story is only useful AFTER the FTS5 mirror has the rows to filter. Ship FIX-01 first. GROUND-TRUTH: read internal/api/wiki.go handleWikiSearch end-to-end (lines 105-186) — the filter has to be threaded through to the search backend OR applied post-hoc in the response loop. Post-hoc is simpler (loop the results, skip system-category ones, top-up to topK if some get filtered out). Pre-filter at SQL is cleaner but more invasive. Pick post-hoc for v0.

userStories.title: Dedupe wiki index by slug across emitters
userStories.description: Witnessed live: `autori-json q2` top-2 hits both have slug=davide, score 0.0262 each. Same slug appears twice in Qdrant. Investigation: is it page-content + graph:node:davide duplicate? Or a stale point that didn't get deleted on rebuild? Or a legitimate dual-emission (page-text + graph-card)? This story: AUDIT first, then FIX. (a) Open Qdrant /collections/aura_memory_v1/points/scroll with filter slug=davide — see the actual records. (b) If two records with different IDs (one `davide`, one `graph:node:davide`), confirm intent: are they intentionally separate retrieval surfaces? If yes, dedup at QUERY TIME via post-filter on slug. If no, fix the upsert path to emit one or the other (not both). (c) If two records with SAME ID (which shouldn't happen with Qdrant's PK), it's an upsert-vs-create bug.
acceptanceCriteria: Commit body documents the audit finding: are davide ×2 the same point twice, or distinct kinds (page+graph-card)?
If distinct-by-design: post-filter at /api/wiki/search dedupes by slug, keeps highest-scored kind, returns each slug at most once in top-k (and the score reflects merge — pick max for now)
If duplicate-by-bug: fix the upsert path; ensure single Qdrant point per (kind, slug)
Test in internal/storage/search/qdrant_test.go (or api/wiki_test.go) verifies dedup behavior
Live bench: 20-query bench output shows ZERO duplicate slugs in any top-5 (today: 1 confirmed in autori-json q2; may be more)
go test ./... -count=1 green
Single atomic commit prefix: fix(qdrant): dedupe wiki search results by slug (US-WIKI-FIX-06)
userStories.notes: AUDIT FIRST. If the audit shows it's an intentional dual-emission (page-content + graph-card both point to the same slug), the right fix is dedup-at-query-time. If it's a bug, the right fix is upsert-side. Don't commit one or the other before reading: (1) internal/storage/search/qdrant.go loadWikiDocuments — does it emit one doc or two per page? (2) The qdrant /points/scroll output for slug=davide. (3) the graph index — does it also push graph cards into qdrant under graph:node:* prefix? SCOPE: if the audit balloons (e.g. a wider 'kind' field architecture), split into FIX-06a (audit doc) + FIX-06b (fix) — keep this story one-commit.

userStories.title: Admin /api/wiki/reindex endpoint + dim-mismatch auto-detect
userStories.description: Two operator-surface infrastructure gaps in one story (related code path). (a) NO HTTP endpoint to force a Qdrant rebuild — today the only path is `cmd/debug_qdrant`, requiring shell access. Add POST /api/wiki/reindex (admin-token gated) that calls RebuildQdrantWikiDocuments + returns the report as JSON. (b) Boot-time dim-mismatch silent failure: today qdrant warm-cache short-circuit (info.PointsCount > 0 → skip rebuild) HIDES dim drift. If operator bumps EMBEDDING_OUTPUT_DIM 256 → 768 without dropping the collection manually, aura silently keeps using the OLD 256d collection (because warm cache hits) and any new upserts crash with dim mismatch at runtime. Fix: at boot, query Qdrant /collections/<name> for params.vectors.size; if != cfg.EmbeddingOutputDim (or native dim when cfg=0), LOG WARN + DROP + RECREATE + REINDEX. Operator can opt out via AURA_NO_REBUILD_ON_DIM_MISMATCH env (defaults to false = auto-rebuild).
acceptanceCriteria: internal/api/wiki.go gains handleWikiReindex POST handler; internal/api/router.go registers POST /api/wiki/reindex (admin-token gated like existing skill admin endpoints)
Response JSON: {collection, points_indexed, pages_indexed, skipped: [{doc_id, reason}], elapsed_ms, vector_size, prior_vector_size}
?dry_run=1 query param: report what WOULD happen (current dim, target dim, points-to-rebuild) without dropping

internal/storage/search/qdrant.go warm-cache short-circuit extended: when CollectionInfo returns vector_size, check against cfg.EmbeddingOutputDim; on mismatch, DROP + recreate + reindex unless AURA_NO_REBUILD_ON_DIM_MISMATCH=true
When Qdrant CollectionInfo does NOT expose vector_size directly (current limitation per WR-03 comment): probe by upserting a sentinel point with the configured dim; if 400 returned, drop+recreate
Boot log: `qdrant collection dim check`, `current=N`, `expected=M`, `action=match|rebuild|skipped_by_env`
Live: UPDATE settings SET value='256' WHERE key='EMBEDDING_OUTPUT_DIM'; docker compose restart aura → collection auto-rebuilt at 256d, no operator action

Single atomic commit prefix: feat(wiki): admin reindex endpoint + boot dim-mismatch auto-detect (US-WIKI-FIX-04)

(2) read internal/api/router.go to find admin-token gated route registration pattern (look for SkillsAdmin).
